newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong invites 60 Taiwanese to handover.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong invites 60 Taiwanese to handover.

text.p: Hong Kong has invited 60 delegates from Beijing's arch-rival Taiwan to celebrate the British colony's handover, apparently with China's tacit approval, officials and diplomats said on Monday.
The delegates included Taipei's official in charge of Taiwan-China reunification talks, but there was no invitation for Taipei government ministers.
With just two weeks left to the handover, China stepped up its gloating at the return of the colony, and small-scale rows about the conduct of the ceremony continued.
At the British garrison, Queen Elizabeth's portrait came down from the wall of the officers' mess.
Diplomats predicted officials from Beijing and Taipei would confer on the sidelines of the gala despite strained ties and the military exercises they both plan later this month.
They said the Taiwan invitations would not have gone out unless Beijing had given at least its tacit approval.
Stephen Lam, the Hong Kong government's coordinator of the handover ceremonies, said the biggest headache in the presence of Taiwanese delegates was where to seat them.

"They are being invited in their personal capacities," Lam said. "As for seating arrangements...if you have done wedding banquets for two or three hundred people, you know how difficult it is, and now we are trying to do one for 4,000 people."

In Taipei, William Li, director of the Hong Kong and Macau affairs department of the cabinet's Mainland Affairs Council, said: "We have approved Straits Exchange Foundation chairman Koo Chen-fu to attend the events."
Koo heads a semi-official agency that handles the Nationalist island's contacts with Beijing, currently stalled.
Taiwan, which calls itself the Republic of China, is the vestige of the Nationalist government that ruled the mainland before 1949 when the communists won a long drawn out civil war.
Britain, China and the Hong Kong government have invited over 4,000 people to an end-of-empire gala banquet and handover ceremony straddling midnight June 30 and the morning of July 1.
Britain's royal heir Prince Charles will hand back the territory to China's President Jiang Zemin.
At the stroke of midnight, China will regain sovereignty over Hong Kong, ending 156 years of colonial rule which began with imperial China's humiliating defeat in the Opium Wars.
China's People's Daily, mouthpiece of the ruling Communist Party, on Monday invoked history to cast aside doubts that Hong Kong had been Chinese territory for centuries.
"The annals of history are evidence that Hong Kong has been Chinese territory since ancient times," the People's Daily said.
"The Chinese government under the leadership of the Communist Party of China had the ability to end the humiliating history imperialists brought on the Chinese nation," it said.
China and Hong Kong are like "hands and feet, blood and tears...Blood is thicker than water", it said.
There was more joy in an article in the official Xinhua news agency on the flood of journalists who have started to arrive.

"Calling it 'the media battle in the century' is by no means an exaggeration now that over 770 media organizations deploy their best contingents equipped with state-of-the-art equipment to capture the historic moment ...." Xinhua said.
China's Foreign Minister Qian Qichen told the South China Morning Post Hong Kong must serve as a bridge to the world.
"China is going to continue economic development and reform, therefore we we still need Hong Kong as bridge and window."
Pro-democracy Hong Kong lawmakers kept up their fight to have their voices heard, protesting against plans to isolate them far away from the main ceremonial action on the handover night.
"It's too many blocks away," said prominent legislator Emily Lau, a seasoned protestor.
